First, let's simplify the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}-2 & \ge 1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6} & \ge 1+2 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{6} & \ge 3 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge 18\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use either of two methods to solve the inequality.

*Method 1 - Solving an Absolute Value Equation*

Taking the square root of both sides of the inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{18} \\ |x| & \ge 3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the definition of absolute value, we must have 

$$
x\le -3\sqrt{2}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 3\sqrt{2}.
$$

So, the solution set is $x\in (-\infty ,-3\sqrt{2}]\cup [3\sqrt{2},\infty ).$

*Method 2 - Picturing a Quadratic Curve*

Starting from ${x}^{2}\ge 18$ and moving all terms to the left-hand side, we reach

$$
{x}^{2}-18\ge 0.
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding parabola given by $\,y={x}^{2}-18\,$ and find its roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-18 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-{(\sqrt{18})}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-{(3\sqrt{2})}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-3\sqrt{2})(x+3\sqrt{2}) & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

hence $x=\pm 3\sqrt{2}.$

Since the leading coefficient of ${x}^{2}-18$   is positive, the parabola  opens upward.  Therefore, the solution set to the  given inequality ($y\ge 0$) lies outside the roots (and  includes them):

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13965374/assets/72488926dd64954e2c1070a94625ebc91c1c729d70bbf7c5f098364e651efec5.png)

Therefore, the solution is 

$$
x\in (-\infty ,-3\sqrt{2}]\cup [3\sqrt{2},\infty ).
$$
